name: Christmas hosts: Crumbles and Frostfoot
picture_standard: This is a host (the friendly-spooky chaser) in a kids' co-op escape game for ages 8 and up: spooky and silly, never gory or truly frightening. For a FRONT view one picture is attached: ANOTHER host from the same game - use it ONLY as a guide to the style, proportions and level of detail; design a completely NEW host from this prompt. For a BACK view one picture is attached: the same host seen from directly behind, same pose, every color the same as the front. Clean, simple 3D cartoon toy style: every area one smooth, flat, solid color, with no texture at all - no fur strands, no crumbs, no cracks painted on, no grime, no wrinkles painted on, no shading or shadows painted on, nothing see-through and nothing glowing (glowing parts become solid bright colors). Simple rounded chunky shapes; small details as simple solid shapes close to the body - nothing thin or long sticking out. A big host, about twice as tall as a 10-year-old. No logos, brand marks, printed words, letters, numbers or graphics. Not like any famous character from a film, cartoon or game. Full body standing in an A-pose: arms straight and angled down and away from the body with a clear gap between each arm and the body, hands open, legs apart, feet flat. Centered and filling the whole height, nothing cropped. Plain flat light-gray background, even soft light, no floor shadow. One character only, no text.
instructions: Run all four assets sequentially in listed order.
Attach every listed reference, resolved relative to reference_root. Front views use Gobbler ONLY for style; each back uses the front generated immediately before it.
Include the entire Picture Standard and exact Picture row in every prompt.
Inspect each reference before generation. Inspect and save each result before advancing.
Create destination folders as needed. Do not overwrite existing artwork without explicit replacement authorization.
The supplied Crumbles rows place the notch on image RIGHT in both views; preserve this explicit per-view placement.
